open_obligations: Compare effect sizes: Arnesen et al. report a 4-point judge-accuracy gain from the SFT model to the final DPO model (p8 L23-25), while Khan et al. report trends against aggregate Elo
Confirm both studies measure debater skill by Elo-style win rates on QuALITY-HARD questions with hidden passages
Check whether Khan et al.'s trend holds for their GPT-4-level debaters, which Arnesen et al. call ambiguous (p10 L16)
out.other_title: Self-play debate: judge accuracy rises with debater aggregate Elo (persuasiveness)
out.rationale: The authors explicitly say their training result matches the trend Khan et al. found with inference-time optimization (best-of-N, critique-and-refinement). How debater skill is raised and which judge is used both differ, so this corroborates the direction of the trend, not its size.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether stronger debaters yield more accurate judges in information-asymmetric QuALITY debate; holds for training-based optimization with one fine-tuned LLM judge

text: The authors state that the positive judge-accuracy trend observed for inference-time optimization of debaters (Khan et al., 2024) persists when debaters are trained, and that it persists even after mitigating judge sycophancy with a trained judge.
title: Arnesen et al. find Khan et al.'s debater-skill/judge-accuracy trend persists with debate training
